title: Kids + Adolescents Research Learning On Tablet Teaching Aachen for children and adolescents with inflammatory bowel disease
summary:
The objective of the CED-KARLOTTA 2.0 study is to implement a digital learning game for German-speaking regions.

The knowledge about inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) of children and adolescents with IBD is tested in an age-appropriate and interesting digital game environment. The game is played by the patients while waiting in the ambulance for their doctor's appointment. In the subsequent contact with the doctor, gaps in knowledge about the disease-specific knowledge are processed. The individual consultation and discussion of the quiz questions are intended to promote a better understanding of the disease.

Inclusion Criteria:
• Female and male children and young adults aged 8-19 years
• Diagnosis of Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis or indeterminate colitis
• Signed consent form
• Patients must be able to read and write German
• Patients must be able to play independently on the tablet

The application is intended to improve specific knowledge and understanding of the disease, adherence to therapy and responsible handling of the disease. In the group of older adolescents in particular, the willingness to make the transition to adult medicine (transition) will be recorded and processed.

In a randomized controlled study with 100 children and adolescents with IBD we want to check the effectiveness (sub-project 1). Our hypothesis is that the additional playing of the Tablet-IBD-Quiz and the individualized counseling have a positive effect on IBD knowledge, disease activity and IBD-related quality of life.

In sub-project 2, the list of questions (IBD-specific questions) is to be tested with 100 children and adolescents with IBD.
